summary: PASS 28/28 (100%). Full backend test suite for the new PDF + Image AI Toolkit ran green on first attempt against the public preview URL. Verified all 8 new endpoints (/api/pdf/info, /pdf/extract-text, /pdf/summarize, /pdf/keypoints, /pdf/ask, /pdf/translate, /api/image/ocr, /image/describe), auth enforcement on every one (401 without Bearer), quota semantics (info + extract-text DO NOT consume quota; summarize + ocr DO consume quota, verified via /api/ai/quota diff), plus regression on /api/auth/guest, /auth/me (valid, missing, bad token), and /auth/session (invalid session_id). Emergent LLM Gemini vision + one-shot flows produced sane outputs (summary contains structure, key-points contain bullets, PDF Q&A correctly answered 'Paris' from planted fact, translation returned Hindi content).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1296 lines — exceeds the 700-line soft cap. Consider splitting AI/PDF/Image routers into their own modules (routers/pdf.py, routers/image.py, routers/ai.py) for maintainability. NOT blocking.

In _gemini_vision (server.py:1208-1225), the `mime` parameter is accepted but never forwarded to ImageContent. emergentintegrations ImageContent auto-detects from bytes so this works today, but the API surface promises mime handling — either pass it through or drop the parameter. NOT blocking; no test failure.

/api/pdf/ask currently increments the quota BEFORE decoding/extracting text. If a user submits an unopenable PDF they still lose a quota unit (raise 400/422 from _decode_b64_bytes / _pdf_extract_text_bytes AFTER quota inc). Consider moving _check_and_increment_quota AFTER the local pre-checks in pdf/summarize, pdf/keypoints, pdf/ask, pdf/translate to make quota consumption fair. NOT blocking, but user-visible.
Auth: get_user_from_token treats naive datetimes as UTC (server.py:63-68) — good. Guest sessions expire in 30 days — reasonable.
PDFFileIn / ImageFileIn have no upper-bound size validation. A very large base64 payload could exhaust memory. Consider adding a max-length check (e.g. 25MB) at _decode_b64_bytes. NOT blocking.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral guest users prefixed with TEST_ created via /api/auth/guest during the run. Consumed a small amount of AI quota (~5 units) on the fresh guest — no persistent artifacts beyond that.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable test file at /app/backend/tests/test_pdf_image_toolkit.py. Uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (falls back to preview URL). Generates its own 2-page PDF via pymupdf and a 500x220 JPEG via PIL at fixture scope (session-scoped so LLM calls run against consistent input). Run with: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_pdf_image_toolkit.py -v --tb=short`. Parallel execution (pytest-xdist) works — 24.7s total wall-clock. Auth flow uses POST /api/auth/guest for a fresh session per run so no seed cleanup required.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found in this iteration. The auth guest-swap regression the main agent flagged is not exercisable purely from backend tests (it's a frontend client-side behavior in /app/frontend/src/api/client.ts and AuthContext.tsx). Backend contract is intact: /auth/me returns 401 (never auto-creates guests), /auth/guest requires explicit POST, /auth/session requires session_id.
